judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration/recital language; the only oddities ('te exercise', trailing 'as follows:.') are transcription noise that changes nothing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It simply introduces the Discovery Period endorsement amendments and sits comfortably with Section III and the Declarations Item 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single dated termination provision; the garbled section cite ('Section XDI') is scanning noise rather than an operative ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 05/13/2009 termination matches the amended Policy Period in the Change Policy Period endorsement (c020) and the Discovery Period dates, so there is no live inconsistency, though the endorsement's own effective date (c008) is the same instant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is a bare pointer to a table; 'shall only apply to the coverages identified below' is definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The incorporated table lists a $160,000 D&O retention that appears nowhere in Declarations Item 9 ($0 / $100,000), a mismatch a court could be asked to reconcile with Section VII(B).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on whether 'the acquiring entity is legally permitted to indemnify the Insured Persons' — an undefined 'acquiring entity' and a legal-permission test that is contestable in a bank-failure setting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels but modifies Section VII(B)(2) (c091), which keys the same retention to the Company rather than an acquirer, so the two retention rules must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement definition of Company hinges on 'the acquiring entity' (never identified) and on 'Wrongful Acts involving the entity or entities set forth in Item 1', a vague coverage boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It displaces the Section IV(E) definition (c042) and feeds directly into the Insured vs. Insured exclusion (c072) and the Insured definition (c047), so its reach is a whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat deletion instruction with no ambiguous term of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It erases the same Section XII that the Mergers endorsement (c179–c181) purports to amend and leave 'unchanged', leaving the status of Section XII(C) genuinely uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain statement that premium is fully earned and the period noncancellable; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the identical sentence in Section III (c037), which is consistent rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective-date statement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It takes effect at the identical moment the Policy terminates under c002, an awkward but conventional sequencing in extended-reporting endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate non-variation language; its meaning is settled and self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Every endorsement repeats it, and it is designed to fit with the base Policy rather than to conflict with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A notice describing claims-made, no-duty-to-defend and defense-within-limits; descriptive rather than operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Section IX(A)(1) and the Limit of Liability provisions, so no divergence between notice and operative text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A numeric aggregate cap; the only defect is a scanning garble ('paovises') that does not alter the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The $10,000,000 total sits against per-agreement limits that in sum exceed it, which Section VII(A)(1)-(2) and the reinstatement clauses (c090(4), c161) must be read with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixed percentage and 365-day length; 'if the eligibility requirements are met' is a cross-reference rather than a vague standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 75% figure squares with the premiums shown on the Discovery Period Activation table and with Section III's calculation formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mailing address; nothing capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section X(C) (c099) points back to this Item, and the two agree.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear condition: no coverage absent a limit, retention and premium in the table.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the Section I lead-in (c031) and governs which endorsement Insuring Agreements are live; consistent throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains a plain miswriting ('HRA/Keogh' for IRA/Keogh) and an odd conditional structure about when coverage 'will be excluded' under Agreement (C).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says Broad Form includes Securities Liability while the table and the Securities Liability endorsement (c165) and Securities Liability Exclusion (c124) treat securities claims separately, requiring reconciliation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sets a $5,000 retention with a garbled cross-reference ('Section ITV (X)(2)'), but the intended reference is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its second sentence sends IRA/Keogh coverage by endorsement to the Item 9 retention, which sits against the Item 11 figure and the reinstatement in Section VII(A)(4).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of endorsement form numbers, partly illegible in transcription, with no interpretive content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The endorsement lists in the successive Declarations amendments (c021, c026) differ from this one, so which forms attach at which date is not perfectly aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional statement of what constitutes the contract and between whom.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks the Policy definition (c054) and the entire-agreement clause (c113), both of which include the Application.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Consideration recital only; no operative term to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It introduces amendments that are internally consistent with the Declarations it modifies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two date ranges stated precisely; nothing ambiguous in the wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The one-month extension interacts with the Policy Year definition (c056), which deems an extension part of the Policy Year ending on the original expiration date — a point that could matter for limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule of form numbers with no interpretive content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs from the earlier and later endorsement schedules (c017, c026), leaving small uncertainty about which forms are attached.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective-date sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It takes effect at the very moment the original Policy Period expired, but that is exactly how the extension is meant to work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-variation boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated verbatim in every endorsement and consistent with the Changes clause (c116).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Consideration recital for a name/address change; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Declarations Item 1 it amends.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of named insureds; the only defect is a scanned typo in a company name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: By putting Vantus Bank first it changes who the 'Named Insured' is under c053, and hence who may cancel, receive notice and act for all Insureds under c104 and c115.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule of forms; no operative ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Differs from the other endorsement schedules (c017, c021), a minor unreconciled variation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective-date sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the sequence of Declarations amendments without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-variation boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Changes clause (c116) and the other endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive notice of the claims-made, defense-within-limits structure; plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with Section IX(A) and Section VII; no divergence between the notice and the operative terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Consideration clause subjecting coverage to all terms; nothing capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Representations clause (c109) which makes the Application the basis of the Policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear precondition to coverage under any Insuring Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates Declarations Item 6 (c014); the endorsement Insuring Agreements (c128, c145, c165) depend on entries in that table, which they have.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The core Side-A grant; 'except for Loss the Company pays as indemnification' and 'legally obligated to pay' are terms that carry real interpretive weight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the Loss definition (c051), the retention rules (c091) and the Insured vs. Insured exclusion (c072), all of which qualify the grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Side-B grant keyed to whether the Company 'has agreed to or is legally permitted or required by law to indemnify', a contestable but conventional trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with the retention rule in Section VII(B)(2) and the deeming provision in Section VIII(A)(2), which are consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Entity coverage grant in short, standard form; the stray 'es' heading is scanning noise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its scope is cut back by Section VI exclusions and the Securities Liability Exclusion (c124), which are expressly directed at Agreement (C).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Numbering is mangled ('a)' then '(2)') and the last sentence uses lowercase 'loss' rather than the defined term, small mechanical defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It extends coverage to estates and spouses in a way consistent with the Insured Person definition; no competing provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'at the direction of the Company' and the excess-coverage proviso are conventional and reasonably determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is deleted for three of the coverages by the Brokerage, Fiduciary and Securities endorsements (c130, c147, c167), so its survival is limited but expressly handled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long provision containing the eligibility trigger, the 'not an extension of coverage' characterisation and the sixty-day election lapse — several phrases parties routinely fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with the Discovery Period Activation endorsement (c002–c008), the Conversion clause (c106) and Item 4, and the Activation endorsement varies its terms in places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sweeping definition reaching materials submitted for 'any Policy of which this Policy is a direct or indirect renewal or replacement'; 'indirect' has an uncertain boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds the Representations and Severability provisions (c109, c110), which depend on what is in the Application.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated definition with an open-ended 'including without limitation' tail and two carve-outs, leaving the outer edge of 'financial planning advice' uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs both the exclusion (c064) and the endorsement Insuring Agreement (c128), which are consistent with each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Whether an 'oral demand for monetary damages or non-monetary relief' has been made, and when, is a classic point of construction in claims-made policies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The date a Claim is 'first made' drives Section X notice, the Single Claim provision (c092) and the Discovery Period deeming rule (c037), so its edges matter policy-wide.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line statutory definition; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the Fiduciary endorsement exclusion (c160); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite by reference to Item 1 and the Subsidiary definition; the 'subject to Section XII (B)' qualifier is a cross-reference rather than a vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section XII(B) is replaced by the Mergers endorsement (c180) and Section XII is deleted outright by the Discovery endorsement (c006), and the same definition is itself replaced by c005.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable and necessary legal fees and expenses' is a familiar standard, with an express carve-out for salaries and overhead.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section IX(B)(2)'s reasonableness verification and the allocation provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Misnames the statute ('Employment' for Employee Retirement Income Security Act), a mechanical error, though the referent is unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in the ERISA exclusion (c067) and the Fiduciary endorsement, which deletes that exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It carves out 'a Leased Employee or Independent Contractor' as capitalised defined terms, but neither is defined anywhere in the Policy, leaving the exclusion's reach uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Employee feeds the Insured Person definition (c048), the undefined carve-out affects who is insured across every Insuring Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A tight two-limb definition tied to appointment of a receiver or debtor-in-possession status; little room for two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the hinge for the retention rules (c091), the Conversion clause (c106), the Insolvency exclusion (c083) and the Insolvency/Bankruptcy clause (c120), which pull in different directions on the effect of receivership.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line composite definition; plain on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is deleted and replaced for fiduciary coverage by c152, and it is what makes the Insured vs. Insured exclusion (c072) bite, so its content is contested indirectly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but enumerated; 'honorary or advisory director' is unusual but determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates the Employee definition with its undefined carve-outs (c045) and drives the Insured vs. Insured exclusion's scope.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of five services with no catch-all; boundaries are reasonably clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in the Insurance Services exclusion (c071) with a matching carve-out for credit life incidental to loans; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Common nexus [of] any fact, circumstance, situation, event, transaction or series of related facts' is famously elastic and its outer boundary cannot readily be applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It controls the Single Claim aggregation rule (c092), the Prior Notice exclusion (c074) and the Subsidiary exclusion (c077), so its breadth reverberates through the limits provisions.
